title: Campus >10x-home assertion is knife-edge against the diff's own cap constants
evidence:
W :: u64(2000)
topology_spawn_node(&s.topology, res_idx, {6, 15}, cat)   // res 0 — sink + email source
topology_spawn_node(&s.topology, res_idx, {18, 15}, cat)  // res 2 — the second sink (dst != src)
topology_spawn_node(&s.topology, camp_idx, {24, 15}, cat) // campus 3 — streaming source
// 5.11: campus — 500 × 150 ÷ 30 = 2500 milli/tick (2.5 pkts/tick, 30× a
// home); ceiling ceil(2.5) = 3 → a ≤3/tick burst (the flood site)
testing.expectf(t, per_role[3] > 10*per_role[0],
		"campus >> home in volume: campus %d vs residential %d (want > 10x)", per_role[3], per_role[0])
append(&e.set_pieces, Set_Piece{id = "streaming_surge", class = 1, multiplier = 10, start_tick = 1200, duration_ticks = 1800, forecast_lead_ticks = 600, archetype_idx = 0})
residential 500×5÷30 = 83 milli/tick (0.083 pkts/tick)
detail: Max campus ~1199 base + 800 surge ticks x2.5 ~ 3200; two homes ~2x2000x0.083 ~ 332, so 10x ~ 3320. Passes only if home credit-overflow losses exceed ~4% — razor-thin, seed-dependent.
recommended_fix: Widen the margin (e.g. >=8x) or derive the expected ratio from the accrue constants instead of hardcoding 10x.

title: PR body describes the golden demo as 'fixture + two spawns'; the demo is fixture-off with seven explicit spawns
evidence:
New `demos/terminal_types.dem` (era 3, growth on, fixture + one small_biz + one campus): captures at 5000 ms and 30000 ms show the three classes as **distinct sprites**
--- demos/terminal_types.dem:
fixture off
growth on
spawn_node router_mid 20 15
spawn_node residential 8 15
spawn_node content_host 32 15
spawn_node residential 14 22
spawn_node residential 26 22
spawn_node small_biz 12 10
spawn_node campus 30 10
detail: The PR description misstates the golden's construction: it is fixture-off with an explicit 7-node layout (router, three homes, host, small_biz, campus), not 'fixture + one small_biz + one campus'.
recommended_fix: Correct the PR body to match the demo file.

title: W9: per-host counters newly gated to SURGE_START but stream_spawned/MIN_LAND left ungated
detail: If the loop is window-only, the new gate is dead code; if it covers pre-surge ticks, stream_spawned mixes base spawns into a check labeled 'streaming window spawns', loosening MIN_LAND.
recommended_fix: Gate stream_spawned identically (or start the loop at SURGE_START) so the counted window matches the assertion's claim.

title: Burst failure message hardcodes ceiling 2 after the check became per-type
evidence:
acc := u64(spawn_credit_accrue_milli(cat, s.topology.node_type[src_slot]))
ceil_cap := (acc + 999) / 1000
if u64(n) > ceil_cap {
	burst_ok = false
}
...
testing.expectf(t, burst_ok, "no per-tick burst beyond the ceiling (2 = ceil_cap) may occur")
detail: The ceiling is now per-type (host 2, campus 3) but the failure text still says '2 = ceil_cap', misleading on a campus-triggered failure.
recommended_fix: Drop the hardcoded 2 or report the per-type ceiling in the message.

title: Era-2 roster loop omits the junction-kind check its era-1/era-3 siblings enforce
detail: era-2's len(r2)==2 + has_small_biz would still pass if a junction (e.g. an era-1 router) replaced residential in the roster; the sibling loops would catch that.
recommended_fix: Add the same kind == .Terminal assertion to the r2 loop.

title: demand.json comment retains 'surge stays x10 the streaming base (10/tick)' after adding a second streaming base entry
evidence: the surge stays x10 the streaming base (10/tick) and lands as an AGGREGATION event across the content_hosts the 5.1 growth has placed by tick 1200. ... 5.11 adds the era-3 entries for the new terminal classes ... + streaming from campus (campuses flood — cap 2.5 pkts/tick, 30x a home; the surge's x10 lands on campuses too, the honest aggregation event).
detail: With two class-1 base entries (content_host + campus, volume 1 each), the surged desired rate is 20/tick, not 10/tick; the retained 5.9 figure now contradicts the appended 5.11 sentence.
recommended_fix: Update the retained 5.9 sentence to reflect the two-entry streaming base.
